So, to the extent that Mr Moran brought up the point that, if they are expert witnesses or document witnesses, he agrees that the reason does not apply, I think we have allayed that. To the extent that there is some other reason, I have not heard the defence articulate it, and I will certainly point out in this case, for instance, all the investigators have had access to all the witness statements of all the defence, because they have been working on this case. So the normal reasons that you would not have one witness hear another witness, which are so that they know what the other witness is going to say and possibly tailor their testimony, are not even applicable. One, these witnesses, there is no possibility that they are going to testify about, in fact, what happened in 1992, and, two, to the extent that there was some sort of fear that they might do something improper, as a result of their knowledge, I must say, given that they have already had access and, in fact, have read, because it is part of their job, all the other witness statements, the reasoning would not apply in that case either. I do not know if I am making myself clear. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Can I hear Mrs Residovic? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, on the list of prosecution witnesses that we are talking about, there are at least three witnesses who could affect the defence of Mr Delalic. You may recall that, before the beginning of proceedings, we proposed the exclusion of one piece of evidence. The investigators, therefore, in my view, should not be present in the courtroom, though we are not opposed to the prosecution calling them up to testify about other events, because it is not always events in Celebici, but there may be events elsewhere. Therefore, if the prosecution wants the investigators to be present in the courtroom, they must tell us exactly the names of those investigators, and then they cannot be interrogated for other circumstances, and, if that is their intent, then in my view, our view, they cannot be present. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, Mr Tapuskovic? MR TAPUSKOVIC (in interpretation): I do not agree that the investigators working on the case should be in the courtroom. I think that the prosecution has its own investigators that can follow in various ways what is happening here, and then to use that for whatever purpose they need. I would agree that our investigators could also be present here somewhere, not necessarily in the courtroom, let them be in the same position as the prosecutors' investigators, because they too, when they hear the witnesses before you, may, in those statements, find something that may serve to help them trace something that may be in the interest of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just if I can briefly respond, with respect to Mrs Residovic, we have given the names of all the potential witnesses, and noted that they may testify, if necessary, on chain of custody issues, or explanation on how given evidence was obtained. I am still not sure if I understand how watching other witnesses might affect that. To the extent that Mr Tapuskovic is suggesting that the same rule apply to the defence investigators, we are not suggesting that there should be a different rule. If the defence wishes to request that investigators, who will not be fact witnesses, be allowed also to be in the public gallery, we would not object to that. We are not suggesting that there should be a different standard for the prosecution. We are suggesting, as Mr Tapuskovic has pointed out, that it is going to be necessary for the investigators to follow in one way or another the course of the proceedings, and the most efficient and really the most sure way is to allow them to, on occasion, hear other witnesses testify, and so that is what we would be requesting. Thank you. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, may I just add that one of the main reasons for the opposition of defence counsel is that the presence of investigators during proceedings, and during testimony of witnesses, may develop negative prejudice among the investigators who may later be heard as witnesses, negative bias about the accused, as well as about what they may be called up to testify about. So that is one of the main reasons for our opposition. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. We have heard the arguments on both sides. I think we sustain the objections. We will give our reasons later. We sustain the objections of the defence. The next is the question of the identity of witnesses, and I think my brother Jan will kindly hand down our decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr President. There are two rules which have a bearing on this subject. There is Rule 61(a)(i), which obliges the prosecution to give the name of the witnesses, which it intends to produce in proof of the guilt of the accused, or in rebuttal of the defence plea, and then there is Rule 69(c), which says the identity of the victim or witness shall be disclosed in sufficient time prior to the trial, to allow adequate time for preparation of the defence. Rule 69(c) is, of course, subject to Rule 75, but then Rule 75 also takes care that the rights of the accused are not prejudiced. Merely giving of names is not sufficient, because there may be persons of the same name, many persons bearing the same name. The identity means much more than that. You have to give enough particulars so that the witness, or the victim, can be identified. It need not necessarily include the present address, but you can give the age, the sex, or any profession of the witness or the victim was following, or the area from which it comes from, so that the defence knows who exactly is the person appearing against him. So the prosecution should provide sufficient particulars, not necessarily the present address, to the defence, in respect of the witnesses. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think that concludes the first stage. We can now proceed with the prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be heard for a second, we have one matter that we would like to be heard before the presentation of the evidence in this case. If you do not mind, after the opening statement by Mr Tapuskovic on behalf of Zdravko Mucic this morning, the defence would like to reurge their consideration for an application for separate trial, and the reasons being there is a motion on file on behalf of defendant Esad Landzo asking the court to do this previously, but before it was only speculation that there would be definite conflicts of interest in the camp of the defence over here. After the opening statement this morning, it has come to fruition there are not perceived differences, but an actual conflict of interest is now visible in the fact that certain admissions by Pavo Mucic now are totally inconsistent with the defence of at least Esad Landzo and I believe a few of the other defendants. At this point, we would like to reurge the motion for a separate trial, based on the fact that there definitely is a conflict of interest. I understand the court's consideration of judicial economy, and we believe that it would not prejudice this court at all, and we could continue with the case, if only Mr Mucic was severed out of the case, so that we could continue with consistent defences. If we are forced to go to trial now with Mr Mucic in here, with totally inconsistent defences from ours, then we are not only countering the evidence of the prosecution, we have one of the co-accused who now is basically only interested in mitigation of punishment at this point, and has basically given testimony contrary to what our defence would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have heard the speech of defence counsel. I do not find any inconsistency between the stance he has taken and your defence. He has merely said that he was not a commandant until 27th July, that his client was, in fact, helping the persons who were being detained here. Where is the inconsistency? The charge against your client is that he has beaten up, killed persons. How is his defence inconsistent with your defence? I would like to be enlightened on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I will do my best. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Excuse me, my understanding is that this motion has been moved before and decided upon. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, on more than one occasion. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I do not think we can go over it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: My only issue was that obvious conflicts have -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: We now hear what you have said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Now you can carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The prosecution now wants to call its first witness, and that is Mr Antonius Beelen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Will it be possible for you to give me a photograph of this model, so that I can carry it to my office, a photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That will be done, your Honour. ANTONIUS GERARDUS FRANCISCUS BEELEN (sworn) Examination-in-chief by MR OSTBERG JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Can you make the announcement for all witnesses to be out of court and out of hearing, please? All witnesses in this case should be out of the Trial Chamber and out of hearing. They should all move out in accordance with our Rule 90(d).

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: As far as I can see, your Honour, everybody has left the room, of our investigators. May I proceed? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Will you please state your name, your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Antonius Gerardus Franciscus Beelen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your present occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a forensic investigator of the Dutch police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are you serving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am serving in the police of Kennemerland, Haarlem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you tell us about how you happened to be given an assignment to do some work for the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a request of the chief of the investigation section of the International Criminal Tribunal to conduct an investigation in the former camp, Celebici. The part of the investigation was to make video films, take photographs pertaining to the investigation, take measurements to create a model, and eventually conduct a forensic investigation within the framework of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you acquainted before you got that assignment with the country, or this place, of Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I never heard of it before. I only -- I know only about the war what I read in the papers, and there was nothing about Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they brief you before you left on what had happened in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told something, that there were kept prisoners, and that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you prepare a report or a booklet, or something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We made an official report, and we made it in Sarajevo shortly after we did our investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And brought it back to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And we brought it back to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your Honour, we are going to introduce Exhibit number 1, and that is the book prepared by the witness during his stay in Celebici. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Will you kindly pass it round to the defence so they can look?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The defence is already in possession of it. There is a copy for each one of you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the Judges receive a copy of this, we would like to express our objections to this document, because there are plenty of inaccuracies in there, and there is prejudicial language that is being used in this document which is inflammatory and would violate Rule 70(d) at this point, as far as highly prejudicial, outweighing its probative value. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually, which is the ground of your objection? Is it the inflammatory language or the inaccuracies? Let us have one?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is twofold. Number one, the renderings in the book itself are not accurate and not to scale. And number 2, the use of language such as "concentration camp", "former Serbian concentration camp" on the documents itself is highly inflammatory and highly prejudicial against the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, these words have been eradicated from the text already.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Not in my copy, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I do not know how that has been done, but we have been going through it, and there is no mention of any concentration camp, or anything like that. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually the word "concentration camp" by itself is not offensive. I think it is very well used all through the world. It is well-known.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the proof of the facility as a former concentration camp is highly prejudicial. They have offered no proof to that whatsoever. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: That is a point of objection I agree with, but one understands that language. It is not new.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: As far as being admitted to the people who are deciding the fact issues in this case, it is highly prejudicial, and we admit to its admission to the fact finders of this case as highly prejudicial, unless proven up, and they have not offered any evidence to prove it up and if it has been removed, I believe we have a right to see the document as it will be admitted to the Tribunal. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us hear Ostberg on the objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you. I cannot accept any objection of the content of the report. That is the witness we are going to examine in this moment and in this court, and he is going to tell the court what he did, what kind of maps, sketches, et cetera, et cetera, he did, and that is the fact of his mission to Celebici, and that is what I am going to bring to this court, to inform it what these premises are like. As to language, I have heard your objections before, and I have taken the initiative to have this word you just referred to being eradicated from the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we certainly have no objections to the witness testifying to the drawings and his investigation of the Celebici facility at all, and, if the document has been altered from what the prosecution has given us to examine, then we would like the opportunity to examine the document as it will be presented to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will have one minute to discuss with my colleagues what measures they have taken, and what it looks like for the moment. Just a moment. Your Honour, when we were informed about this objection, we took it out of the documents to lead to it being introduced as an exhibit, but we have supported the defence beforehand with the these documents in Serbo-Croat and in English, if I remember correctly, and there these now objected to words are still there, but these words are taken out of the copies now given to the court as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we appreciate the fact that they are accommodating our request, but we would like the opportunity now to inspect the documents that will be distributed to the Tribunal. We have not had a chance to see the modified documents. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually, you are not objecting to the expertise of the witness and what has been produced as a competent document, you are not objecting to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: We have not heard anything to prove that he is an expert at this point, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I thought you would have started from that, instead of objecting to areas which perhaps could easily be cleared.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr Ostberg has just requested that a document be distributed to the Tribunal for its inspection, and, before the Tribunal receives this document -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You have gone on to talk about the content of the document, without even referring to the expertise of the person who produced it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is highly prejudicial and has nothing to do with the investigation of the camp itself. The label on there has nothing to do with what the dimensions are of the camp whatsoever. It has nothing to do with this so-called non-fact witness that they have put on, and the introduction of the language that he has put in here is highly flammable and has nothing to do with his examination as an unbiased investigator of the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You will have the right to cross-examine him and you can ask him about these terms, you can ask him about his lack of knowledge. You can ask him about -- you have the right to cross-examine him, and you can bring out evidence from his own mouth showing that he is not an expert, he has used expressions he ought not to have used and that there are inaccuracies in his report. So at this stage your objection has not been well-founded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: We are voicing our objections to the Tribunal being able to view this inflammatory statement and the ruling is overruled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have noted your objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: We are really not a jury. We can discriminate between what ought to be taken into account and what should not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I guess you can see that I have tried too many jury trials. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: On the other hand, I have never tried a jury case. May I proceed to examine my witness? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Then will you tell us in summary how you produced this document? Did you make some kind of a summary in your document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you briefly, briefly summarise your summary, just to tell the court what it led up to -- your findings -- before we go into photos and sketches, and things like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I made a description of the situation we saw out there in Celebici. When we were there in October last year, we first had an impression of the total camp, and then, after that, we took photographs, made video films, made measurements. During the night of the same day, we all put our material in the computer and worked it out as an official report, as you see before you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say "we". That means that you were not alone there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was there with a colleague, Hendrik Post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that name appear on the proces-verbal you have in here, on page 1 in our Exhibit number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did this together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did this together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you go on with your summary, or is that enough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you go on with your summary, or this is enough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is enough. And you said you made sketches, and may I now turn to page 4 -- no, I start with page 3. This is a sketched overview of the camp. Did you make that sketch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at this, there are letters and numbers of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We do not have these books. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us have them for identification first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, your Honour. You have the original of your booklet there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the one you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is one of the ones, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the book as the whole that you have in your hand now. Is that the one you prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Tender it for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: So now I tender this as our Exhibit number 1, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: For identification at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: As far as I understood, the witness has now identified it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. You have now identified this book as the one you produced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: After this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I do not need a photograph now with these detailed sketches, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour. Now I will direct you, Mr Beelen, to page 3 in this booklet, and I will ask your Honours also to get to page 3, which is the same -- 3A is a bigger sketch and the smaller one to make it more feasible is on page 3. Did you make that sketch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you put these numbers and letters on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To give all the buildings a name, we put a letter on it, and it is from A to N, and we also made some measure points on the map, 1 to 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a key to your measuring of the facilities, of the buildings in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I do not understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a key or a list of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is on page 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 9. Will you describe for us what we can find on page 9, when the court has reached page 9?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On page 9, there is the letter we gave to the building, A, the name of the building, what it was at the moment we were there, and the measurements of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notify the video people, so we can also see all these things on the screen before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour, but the pages you are referring to do not seem to match. When you say page 9 and page 3, they do not match in our booklets. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You do not have page 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This foldout map is page 1 in our booklet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is 3A.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It is page 1 in ours. That is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Then of course to get over that hurdle, we put the thing on the ELMO, so we can all see what we are talking about. This was given to the defence beforehand and after that there had been, for technical reasons, some kind of a renumbering. We will see to it, but you have exactly the same thing. There must be some confusion about the pages, which I was not aware of. May I just explain to the court, the defence has exactly the same copy. The only thing that differs due to some technical things is the numbering of the pages, and there is the confusion. But we will soon have it in the computer system, so we can all see the same thing when we speak about it. Your Honours, this is now all in the computer system, so I will now ask the computer people to bring us to page 3. There we all see the map, which also is in the book. Again, I will ask Mr Beelen to tell us something about what he did to make it possible for the court to identify the different buildings and things in the Celebici facility.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One point of our mission was to make a sketch of the total camp, because they wanted to make a model of it. As you see, it is a fairly large camp, so we pointed four points on the camp, 1 to 4, from where we took our measurements. So you can see the total length of the camp, from point 2 to point 3, is 485 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and then you numbered or named the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, then we gave all the buildings a letter, from A to N, letter A to N, because the buildings were numbered by the users, but there were several buildings with the same number on it. There were three number 6s, and it is very disturbing, so we made them a letter A, B, D, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We also see that, apart from numbers, and letters, some of the buildings also have names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you get these names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were names given us by the local users of the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that takes me to the question, what was this facility used for when you visited there in October 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camp was used as an oil storage, a liquid store, a gas oil station, and it was, how do you say it, a storage for oil products.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was by no means any longer some kind of a prison or a detention, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was running this facility when you visited it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of military people? What army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came up with numbers from, as you said, from A to O?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: N -- O, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it is O?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the last one is O.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A to O. Then, if we turn, and I ask now also the computer people to go to page 4, did you make sketches even of the different buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We made sketches of the buildings A, B, C, and E, a hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 4, which is now on our computer system, is there a letter attached to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is building A. It is the guard house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made also a sketch, if we go now over to page 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 5 is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment. We will ask the computer people to follow us. Thank you. What is on page 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 5 is the administration building, named as B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your sketch, does it show all the rooms that were in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are rooms which were there at the moment we were in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these names, technician, commander, toilet, room with bed, et cetera, is that exactly how it was when you visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is when we visited there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that has nothing to do with its former capacity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is just as it was when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask the computer assistant to give us page 6? What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 6 is building C, and it is a store house for water pumps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have the size on it also here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we have the size on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they as empty as they appear on the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were some pumps in it, and a bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you to go to page 7, and also the computer? I hope the defence can follow us without difficulties. You can find these things without difficulties? Very good. What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is building A, hangar number 6, as the military call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Hangar, the answer was hangar. Why the name hangar? Is there any explanation to that fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a warehouse, and at the moment we were there, there were fuel barrels inside of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any explanation why they used the word "hangar"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is how they called it, the local people, hangar number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without any special explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Not for aeroplanes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: No, there was no aeroplane in it, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were some oil barrels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask the computer to go to page 8? What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 8 is building number O, and the local people called it tunnel number 9. It is a very long tunnel, 30 metres long, and it was partly underground, and in it was an operation room and a pump room for the oil storage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again we can see the length and the width and the height of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as I can read here, it was 30 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30 metres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The width was 1 metre 50 and height 2 metres 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you any idea what this tunnel was used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was part of a distribution station of the oil storage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than oil?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fuel tanks underground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were the buildings of which you made special sketches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you made sketches of just these buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me there were explanations about these specific buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were asked to make sketches of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the people who tasked you to go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr Beelen, you also took photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We took photographs of the total camp, and especially from the buildings which you saw the drawings from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now will you please take us through these photos, and I will now ask the computer assistants to help us and go to photo -- the first photo, page 10?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is photo 1. You see a total view of the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name one of the buildings for us, so we get acquainted with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The building you see in the middle is building A, I think, building F and building G, from left to right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this taken from the direction from the entrance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the end of the camp, but I should not use that word now, because it is not a camp any more, from the entrance of this facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the bottom of it to the entrance, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next picture, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next picture is taken from the same place, but a little bit more to the right. So you see building G, building H, and a part of building F.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next picture, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next picture is taken from the same place, and it is the last building on the camp, building G.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I can see, there is a railway going in the middle of the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, between --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the rail inside or outside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the photograph, you see the rail is outside, and between building F and building G, it is coming into the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next picture, please. What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the main gate of the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taken from inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Taken from inside to the outside, yes. At the right you see the guard house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next picture, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next picture is another shot of the guard house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a view of the guard house opposite to the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have photo number 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the administration building. To the left, at the end, is a hangar which they do not use any more. It was kind of in repair for motor cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also called hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the right you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And right you see building C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the letter of this building, or number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The building to the right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is building C, the store house for water pumps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember the sketch, can you remember which number this building, the small building to the right, had for the local people there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have a look on the first sketch on page 3, if we can have page 3 again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is building C, but I do not know which number the local people gave it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is just -- for you, it is just building C?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot remember if there was a number on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then we go on, please, with picture number 8.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the main entrance of the administration building, building B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And let us have a look at picture number 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the administration building again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 10?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And it is the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From another angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, seen from building D.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 11?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the back side of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we come to number 12.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 12 is the inside of the administration building. Just from the main door, looking inside to the toilets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let us go to number 13.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 13 is the toilet room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 14?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 14 is a view from the, how do you call it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All photographs are from the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: We go now to number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a room which is under repair. They were painting it, and it is not a specific room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 16 is the room of the commander in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And number 17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the room of the technician, the technolog, as they call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was on the outside of the door, the word "technolog"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on the outside, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we are still in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 18?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 18 was kind of a radio room opposite the room of the technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. 19?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 19 was a room with a bed in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 20?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20 was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are still talking about the administration building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Still in the administration building. It is another room with a bed in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: And 21?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 21 is a view of the cantina in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And 22 is a look at the kitchen, which is just between the cantina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also in the same building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, and that way we leave the administration building and look at picture number 23.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what we call building C. It is the store house for the water pumps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your list of the pictures on page 10 -- can we have page 10, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: 10. That is an index of the photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For this building, called building C, is that the same as on picture 23?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you call it in your index "dispensary"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you call it "dispensary"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we get our mission, they told us this building was used as a dispensary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your people in the investigation office, in the prosecutor's office, who sent you out --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- told you something, and said that this was the dispensary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So therefrom you have the name. You do not have it from people now running this facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is correct. The local people called it just a store house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we go back, please, to 23, picture 23, please. There we are again. Now we have the clarification of its name in this index. Please, number 24. Is that the same building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the same building, but the backside of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we go to number 25.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 25 is the same building, but then the inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 26?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is another part of the inside from the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. 27?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 27 is a view of two holes opposite a little hill, a small hill, along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have a letter for that building in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no letter on it. On our map we called it "checkpoints".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Let us go to 26, and you will tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 28, I beg your pardon. I misread the number. 28, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 28 is what we thought was a checkpoint too. It is a kind of guard post, or an observation post, and all the wood was maybe from a kind of a shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And number 29?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 29 is the first hangar, building E.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the word "hangar", again, was that used by the local people you met there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember if this hangar on picture 29 had some local number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hangar number 6, building E.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a plate on it, or something saying it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a sign number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We cannot see it from the picture, can we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, the yellow one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but we cannot see the number 6 somewhere. Was it put on the other side of the house, or where did you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- the yellow sign you see in the middle of the building, on that is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Orange colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Orange colour, that is correct. And that was number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We go now to number 30, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 30 is the same building, with the inside of it. You can see the oil barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We go to 31.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 31 is the same building, and the photo shows five bullet holes in the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see a small door, and this is a part of a bigger door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is part of a bigger door, which they can open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see some brown spots on the picture. Did you examine these holes yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, as a police officer, say that these were bullet holes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, these were bullet holes, but they were there a long time, because they were all rusty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are certain that it was bullet holes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 32 does not exist, I suppose, so we go to 33.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. 33.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 33, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 33 is a view of building F and building G.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the one we just looked upon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we also see this orange sign in the middle of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which bore the number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes, it would be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We see -- I am sorry, I said it wrong. We see building G and building H.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Building G is the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the front you see the railway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The railway is crossing in the middle of the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the buildings are again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Building G and building H, and building G was also called hangar number 6, 6B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 34, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 34 is the railway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inside the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Inside, and it is passing behind building F.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And 35?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 35 is another view of the railway, inside the camp. The building you see is building A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the small one in the centre of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the large one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The small one, does it have a number, or something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not put it on the map. Along the small one are the checkpoints, or the shelters we saw before, just above it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the grass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. 36, please. Are we still inside the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are still inside in the area, and this is the end of the railway looking to the direction of the main gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. 37?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the last building on the area, building G, hangar number 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these yellow or orange signs we have seen on some pictures, you did not put them there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were there. They pointed number 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On picture number 38, what is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a concrete structure, building K we called it, and there is a cover on the top, from which you can go inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you go inside, where do you get then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then you come down to a small area, with a very strong smell of fuel, and in it there were steps and fuel pipes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this connected with something else, or it just goes down in the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was just in the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And there were pipes going to a storage tank, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these -- are these -- I see two pipes on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two pipes were for fresh air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Picture number 39, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 39 is the cover of that structure building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that we just saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the concrete one, the top of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 40?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the same building, now the cover opened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it takes you just down, so you cannot go underground --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can go, it is about two metres in depth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we have two pictures. Is it from the inside, both of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is from -- we were standing on the top of it and taking down. It is photo number 41.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we have photo 41, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taken from --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the upside to downside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 42?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also taking from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Taken from up to down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we go to 43.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 43 shows us particularly underground store rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are these the entrances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the entrances of two buildings, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underground buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Underground buildings. We call them both building L.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They have the same letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We call them the same letter, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they connected these two, underground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were called hangar number 7, both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hangar number 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remember, still talking about picture number 43?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 44, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 44 is a picture of a large fuel station. We called it building N. It is a gas oil station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Along the rail, is there a rail passing behind it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The rail is to the right of the road. There is the railway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of the road is the railway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 45?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the entrance of tunnel 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the word "tunnel 9", were you given that by the local people when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was given by the local people. You can see the sign number 9 on it, and we called it building O.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can all read this sign number 9 on the door. This door is leading where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This door is leading to a tunnel, 30 metres long, and it is underground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we turn to 46. Can you explain what you see on 46?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 46 you can see the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a view to the entrance of the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it taken from the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is from the inside to the outside, to the door with the sign number 9 on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what we see in the centre of the picture is the door that we just saw from the outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good. Number 47?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 47 is taken from the same place as the photograph before, but now to the inside. This is the door leading to a large -- not a large, a little room at the end of the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, and 48?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 48 is the entrance of the little room down in the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we go to 49.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 49 is inside, at the end of the tunnel. It is a large room with pumps from --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the inside of the room to which we saw the doors on the foregoing picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a room between it. You can see it on page 8. You can see the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go to page 8, please, if our computer assistants can take us to 8 again, that is a sketch of the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the sketch of the tunnel. You can see the operation room, and the pump room as we saw before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The pump room is on picture --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is photo picture 49, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please, to picture number 50.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 50 is at the outside of the tunnel, just above the pump room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the pump room, is this the concrete building in the centre of the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, it is a kind of a manhole, which leads down to the pump room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can get into the tunnel through stairs down from this entrance --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the concrete building. The other things on the picture, what shall I call it, pipes or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All kinds of pipe, for air for the oil storage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have not numbered them and given them letters or something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this concrete building, you give that a letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it was all a part of tunnel 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a part of tunnel 9, thank you. And now we go to photo number 51. What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 51 is the end of the railway at the right, and to the left you can see a wall, which was the opposite side of the whole area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what we see is that the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main gate of the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see the gate and we see also the gatehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the rail -- the rail went all the way up there, this tank thing is standing on rails?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is on a rail, and it was the last part of the railway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then we come to the last picture, number 52, please. What is this, and why do we have it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a view of the wall, and there was damage on the wall which had been repaired with new cement, and the damage could be caused by projectiles, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is something you believe, or suppose, or something you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now we know it was used for -- they were damaged by bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could establish that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That has taken us through this booklet, with its sketches, its photos and its lists of buildings. Do you have more to add concerning this booklet, or whatever I could call it? Do you have any comments to add to what you have said so far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I thank you very much for that. That, your Honours, takes us to have a look at the model standing in the centre of this courtroom. Having looked at the pictures you have already an idea of what it looks through a camera lens, and now you will have to look at it as a model. The first question is, however, to you, Mr Beelen: did you prepare this model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not prepare it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was prepared by the Centrale Werkplaats Instructiemiddelen. It is a part of the Dutch army, and they made it by our measurements and our photos and video film.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you supervised its production?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And controlled it and measured it, and it was done after your instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was done after all my instructions, and when we were back in Holland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is it made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was made at Breda in Holland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the Dutch army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will ask you to -- I do not know how we make this from the point of view of recording what you say. Can you, from the place where you are, maybe, describe the model for us? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you need something to point with? Maybe somebody could support you with that. Could we have some support from anybody, the usher, or somebody, to give us a pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will do it with this pen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think a pen is a rather short instrument. This may be better. Just before you start, I would like now, your Honours, to tender this model as an evidence in the trial, and I call it Exhibit number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object to this being offered and accepted into evidence at this time. We have not had a chance to prove up that it is not authentic and it is not to scale, and it is not appropriate to be used as evidence. I know that right now they are using it just for demonstrative purposes, but as a piece of evidence in this case, and we have the right to at least take him on voir dire and find out how accurate this is. So we object to it being admitted into evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: And I object to the objection. I would ask Mr Beelen to show his model. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You are being asked to justify your tendering it. That is all the objection is. How do you justify your tendering it through this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I tender it through this witness, because it is made up under his instructions by personnel of the Dutch army, and he is responsible for it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He is not the maker.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: He is not the maker, but it is made under his supervision, after his photos, after his measurements, and he has supervised its production, so I am prepared, your Honour, to submit to you that he is the person responsible for the production of this model we see before us. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He has not said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: He has not said so? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: No, he said it was not made by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: It was not made by him, but I think I expressly asked him if it was made under his supervision. That is, in my submission, enough to make him responsible for the production. Even if he did not do it by his own hand, he had it done after his instructions, and how could it else be done? I do not know what I can do, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond, before its acceptance into evidence, the defence would like an opportunity to challenge his specifications, the authenticity of the measurements here and at least have the right to challenge it before it is accepted into evidence. We have no objection to it being used for demonstrative purposes, until we get a chance to challenge it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Well, challenge, then. Ask him your questions, and let him see whether he cannot answer them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I was waiting for cross-examination, but if you would like for me to take -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: In respect of it being tendered, if you want it not tendered, you have to put to him the objections why it should not be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: We know for a fact that, based on our photographs and video tapes that we have also, that there are inaccuracies about the train tracks going toward the front of the building, that there are inaccuracies on the elevation of the hill between building known as number 22, the dispensary and hangar number 6, and we would like to at least have the opportunity to prove up those inaccuracies before it is admitted into evidence. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually, I am not too sure, I am not an expert on this, but you have two measurements you are not taking on the same scale, is it? Your own photographs and his own are not on the same scale?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, it will prove that their scale is wrong. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Everyone has his own scale which he takes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe we can mark it as number 2 for the time being and after the examination is over, let us put it as Exhibit 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I would like to ask one question to the witness before doing so, which might clarify the position. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us clear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour. Then I will ask you, Mr Beelen, can you testify before this court that this is a fair and accurate description, this model, and that it answers up to the facts that you gave the people who manufactured it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I gave them all my original materials, all my measurements, all my original video tapes, all my original photographs, and they have instruments to make a model from all those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To you, Mr Beelen, is that, this model, a true picture for you of what it looked like in this compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. It is a real, true picture of what I saw when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Now I ask to tender this as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let us mark it as Exhibit 2 because of the objection and after the cross-examination is over, we can exhibit it as Exhibit 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Absolutely. It suits me perfectly, thank you, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think the Trial Chamber will rise for fifteen minutes, and when we come back, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you. (4.05 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can continue, Mr Ostberg.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I ask the usher to bring in the witness again? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You are still on your oath, as you swore when you started.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I put any questions to Mr Beelen, I would like to explain to the court and to the defendants and to the defence counsel, and to Mr Beelen, that this camera standing beside the model has the facility or possibility to move from building to building to building, so, instead of a pointer, which we had a problem to find, in this court, it is possible for Mr Beelen to just name the letter, and then the camera will go to the different things, and I do not know if we need somebody to operate this camera from inside the courtroom, or from the box, I do not know which. Someone is coming, I believe. Thank you. Please, Mr Beelen, will you please just briefly again explain how this model was manufactured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The model was manufactured by a specialist from the Dutch army and they made it by our measurements, or photographs, and our video films, all unedited, so they have every material we took down there in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now added to the model is two other pieces, one to your right side, and one to your left side. Will you just explain to the court what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are larger buildings, building A and building B. Building A is the guard house, and building B is the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is just an enlargement of two of the buildings on the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Made at the scale of -- how much bigger are they? 5, 6, 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not make them by myself, so I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are just bigger models of two of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the buildings on the model.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good indeed. Now we will see if the camera is ready to -- does it work now? Fine. Then I will ask you, Mr Beelen, having in mind that we have shown the sketches, having in mind that we have looked at the pictures, now describe the model for us again, tell us what is what on the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The model shows us the complete military camp, as we saw it down in Celebici. Every building which we saw is on it, every hill we saw is on it, every hole we saw is on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will you now, starting from the entrance, go through the different buildings? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Excuse me, it is not appearing on the screens, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Is it there? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Everyone is using the video monitor, are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Now we all have it on our screens? Thank you. Then I will ask you to proceed in this way, that you start from the entrance gate and go through the building. When you do it, I would be glad if you also give the names you have given them beforehand and the numbers that appeared on these different buildings. Will you please do that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you can just use the camera and the camera operators as your pointer, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will. At the right on your monitor you see the main gate, and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up in the right corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there it is. When you enter the gate, then you see the guard house on your left, marked as building A, and, when we turn to the left, we come to building B, and on site of it, building C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name them now from how they were named when you were there also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Building B was the administration building. Building C was what they first called dispensary, but what was a store house for pumps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the other side of the monitor you see building D. Building D was just a hangar for repair of motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we go to the left, to the long road, and then you go up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That follows the fence? Does it go along the fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it just goes here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this road you just said we were following, is that also going along the fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We see a large grey hole in the hill. It is an oil filtering installation, where all the rainwater is coming together and they filtered oil out of it, so that the water is fresh again. Just above it you can see two holes in the hill. They were the guard posts, the shelters, which we saw before on photo. Then the first building you see is hangar 6, building A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Building E?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Building E, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Building E?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Building E.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hangar number 6. Behind it is building F, hangar number 21, and along it, it is the railway from the entrance of the camp to the oil storage, gas oil station. Higher up, you can see building G and building H.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have it focused so we can read the G, fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Building G.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is G, yes. Did that have another number also, building G?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Building G was also hangar number 6, 6B. Above it you can see building H, hangar number 20, as the local men called them. Then you can go further. At the end of the total military camp you can see building J, hangar number 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we have gone all the way, all the 485 metres from the entrance gate to the end of the facilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from exactly 485 metres from point 2 till point 3, and point 3 was a point given by us just in the left corner of your monitor. It is not on the model.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we focus on this grey thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The grey thing is building K. It is the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concrete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The concrete massif with the cover on it and oil, the air pipes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the background we see the fence at the end of the facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
